bull.probability_evidence: Bull case lists every multiple below its 5y minimum and the peer median (EV/EBITDA 6.6x vs 8.1x min/8.6x peers; P/FCF 9.9x vs peers 11.8x; FCF yield 10.11%) plus rising FCF conversion (117% TTM) and ongoing buybacks (shares -3.24% YoY) [Certain], but the evaluator caps conviction at 3/5 and tags the re-rating trigger 'Guessing' ('Stable returns alone could lift the multiple back toward its 5-year floor [Guessing]') because five years of falling ROIC/gross margin are unresolved - weighted below base and bear for that reason.

target_band.cite: Fact sheet Valuation table (RA): re-rating the bull story's 'returns stabilise' thesis to each multiple's own 5y minimum gives three different implied prices from current close 57.07 - P/E 12.5x->12.8x: 58.44; EV/EBITDA 6.6x->8.1x: 70.03 (the evaluation's own basis); P/FCF 9.9x->13.1x: 75.52. Spread 75.52-58.44=17.08; half-spread 8.54; band = 8.54/70.0 = 0.1220.

base.probability_evidence: Evaluator's own rationale gives the base case the modal weight: 'Valuation and cash conversion are attractive, but the thesis needs returns to stabilise... show no sign of that yet' - i.e. the current slow-erosion-offset-by-FCF-yield/buybacks pattern (base scenario basis) continuing is the single most likely path, consistent with the AVOID/conviction-3 decision (neither a high-conviction re-rating nor an acute break).

target_price_12m.cite: evaluation.md Decision json: scenarios.base.target_price_12m = 59.0, basis 'Multiples stay near P/E 12.5x as slow ROIC erosion offsets the 10.11% FCF yield and 3.24% share shrink'

target_band.cite: Fact sheet Valuation table (RA): the base basis holds the multiple at its current level (P/E stays at 12.5x, no re-rate). Applying the same 'multiple unchanged' assumption to EV/EBITDA (6.6x) and P/FCF (9.9x) gives the identical implied price (current 57.07 plus the FCF-yield/buyback uplift to 59) as the P/E anchor - the three anchors agree exactly, so there is no anchor-disagreement band for the base case; no second valuation anchor is cited for base beyond 'stay near P/E 12.5x'.

bear.probability_evidence: Bear case cites concrete, already-in-train deterioration rather than a hypothetical: ROIC down every year to 14.8% TTM, gross margin down to 33.4% [Certain]; Piotroski F only 4 [Certain]; net debt/EBITDA moved from net cash (-0.19x) to 0.26x 'as bolt-on M&A begins' [Certain]; and the macro overlay notes real yields +48bp/1m cap any re-rating [Likely] (research/CTSH/2026-10-08-macro.md). This concrete evidence outweighs the bull case's single 'Guessing'-tagged re-rating hope, so bear is weighted above bull.
